docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:34:3. **AC-3 — `secretRef` end to end.** A declared `<secret ID>` classifies to `sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:ID}`; an undeclared ID is `FORBIDDEN_SCOPE`. The model receives the step text with the token span masked plus the reference (the ID), never a value: a gateway spy asserts the outbound bytes contain the ID and zero planted-value bytes (SEC-1). Materialization adds `authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId}` with no value, hashed into `authoredInputsHash`. The learned plan and lowered artifact carry `fill.value={kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}` and `inputRecipes[inputId]={kind:secretRef, referenceName:ID}` — the **only** spelling of a secret use on the single path — and `artifactHash` is identical before and after a Vault rotation (SEC-8). `validator/observedReplay.ts` and `ObservedRevisionVerifier` refuse any artifact whose fill literal equals a declared secret's resolved value and any `authoredLiteral`/`sourceSpan` overlapping a `<secret …>` token. [design §2, §3 "Reference rule"]
docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:36:4. **AC-4 — Right moment: step binding (I-A1).** A secret is filled only (a) at a step whose authored source declares it, (b) in slot `fill.value`, (c) into the unique password control of AC-5, (d) on an origin in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins` whose owning `form.action` origin is inside `allowedOrigins`. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts a `passwordControl` target only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; `executionEvidence` document/generation staleness checks are unchanged. Runner `guided/runtime.ts` insists `input.sourceStepId === coordinate.stepId && intendedSlot === slot` for `secretRef` as it does for `authoredLiteral`; `validator/observedReplay.ts` and the observed executor re-check `inputRecipes[].stepId` at validation and at `perform` (`REFERENCE_MISMATCH`). The artifact-1 binding in `validator/references.ts` is **not** cited as evidence (it leaves with OBS-012A). [design §4.6 I-A1; §4.2; §4.3; oracle C-1]
docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:38:5. **AC-5 — Trusted password-control resolution (security condition 1, tightened by R1-1/R1-2/R1-3).** The model never sees a password node (the collector does not export them). "Visible, enabled `input[type=password]`" is defined **once** in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots, frames and closed shadow roots excluded — and that single function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll('input[type=password]')` resolver outside it is forbidden (static test, C-20). Resolution runs inside the collector's isolated world under the existing `acquire`-style guard (cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call); the element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world and the fill requires the **same element** still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique candidate, with `location.origin` read in-world (not `page.url()`) inside `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill (C-18). 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing typed; off-screen rendered decoys count (⇒ refuse), iframe/closed-shadow inputs do not (⇒ absent ⇒ refuse). A pinned input whose owning `form.action` resolves to an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or a form-less input on a document whose origin differs from the observed login document, ⇒ `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED`, nothing typed (C-19). **Limit (ADR-SC-005 default, no opt-out):** multi-password pages and secrets into non-password controls are unsupported for `secretRef` fills at GA — `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`/`POLICY_DENIED`, nothing typed, no fallback adapter; stated in the runner README. [design §4.2, §4.3; security review "R1 delta check" R1-1, R1-2, R1-3; oracles SEC-6, C-18, C-19, C-20; ADR-SC-005 defaults "Secrets"]
docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:50:9. **AC-9 — Backend sinks (I-B4, F-4).** A final `SecretValue` type wraps `char[]`, prints `<secret>` from `toString()`, has no Jackson-visible getter and is written only by one explicit writer (`JsonGenerator.writeString(char[],int,int)`) used by the two secret-bearing serializers (`HttpRunnerDispatchClient` body, guided `BridgeDispatch` builder) and replay `job()`, erasing after write; `RunJob.resolvedSecrets: Map<String,String>` and `text(resolved.secrets())` are replaced. The Vault read is parsed with a streaming `JsonParser` (`getTextCharacters`) straight into `char[]` — the secret path never calls `ObjectMapper.readTree`; bodies are published as `byte[]` (`ofByteArray`) and zeroed after send (test seams for both). Oracle C-5: with root and `com.citi.put.checks` at TRACE and every appender captured during a two-path controlled run (guided learn, observed replay), zero canary hits in logs, problem+json bodies, SSE frames, `/actuator/prometheus` and the `IdempotencyFilter` cache; `RunJob.toString()`/`SecretValue.toString()` print no value. Residuals (JVM `String` copies, Jackson/`HttpClient`/TLS buffers) are documented in the evidence file, not asserted. [design §4.6 I-B4, I-A2 read/write residuals; security condition 4]
docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:74:18. **AC-18 — `LOGIN_REQUIRED` on guided learn and observed replay (design R3 §5).** An annotation of a failure that already happened — it never turns a passing step into a failure or vice versa — with `detail:{stepId, loginStepsPresent}`. Signature S(observation), trusted code only, one function for both paths: `coverage.passwordControls ≥ 1` **and** an exported visible actionable node with `elementType ∈ {button, input}` or `role === 'button'`. Guided: `GuidedTranslationService` fires it when the step's attempt ended in a validator rejection, `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`/`MISSING_SOURCE`, or a `passwordControl` fill proposed without a `secretRef` input, **and** S holds; `loginStepsPresent` = a `secretRef` fill was dispatched earlier in the session; session → `FAILED`, `failure.code = LOGIN_REQUIRED`. Replay: `executor/observedReplay.ts` via the observed adapter, on the action that ends the run with `TARGET_DRIFT` or `POLICY_REFUSED`, when S(that observation) holds and the failing action is not itself a `secretRef` fill; `loginStepsPresent` = an earlier `secretRef` fill was performed; reported as `errorCode LOGIN_REQUIRED` with `detail:{stepId, loginStepsPresent}` in `x-runner-error-codes`; the run stays `FAILED` and the drift step is still named for "Learn again" (OBS-015). After login steps the next observation is of the reached document; login-page evidence is never reused for protected-page controls. False-positive limits (registration/change-password/CVV pages; custom forms without `type=password`; SSO on non-approved origins blocked earlier) are documented; localized button text is not used. Oracle (§7 "§5" row): `/reports` without login steps ⇒ `{loginStepsPresent:false}`, wrong password ⇒ `{true}`, registration page with passing assert ⇒ no annotation — on guided; the same three on a published plan with the fixture session expired between learn and replay. [design §5; §7 "§5" row]
docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:78:19. **AC-19 — Controlled fixture and executed oracles.** A local fixture serves `/login` (cookie session), `/home`, `/reports` (protected), `/echo`, `/trap` (type flip on focus), `/two-passwords`, `/no-password`, `/slow`, `/spa-swap`, a same-origin page whose password form `action` resolves cross-origin, and an open-shadow-root login form. Every design §7 oracle placed in this story is implemented and executed through the actual backend/PostgreSQL/Core-HTTP/runner/Chromium path: SEC-1…SEC-10, §5 (three cases × two paths), rotation/revocation/isolation, end-to-end, C-1…C-7, C-11…C-20; C-8, C-9, C-10 and the manual video-masking inspection are OBS-009. End to end: `<var USER>`/`<secret PASS>` → login → protected assert → publish → two replays with distinct fixture receipts and identical `artifactHash`; video of the **replays** present with masked dots (first-Run video is OBS-013); both gateways silent during finalize and replay. Existing Studio regressions are rerun: OBS-006 joined tests (`GuidedPublicationReplayIT` and siblings), `confinement.test.ts`, `NoRuntimeLlmTest`, `DeReadyCarryForwardTest`, runner default/fixtures/deployment tiers; compile-path suites are rerun unchanged (they are deleted by OBS-012A, not by this story). No unavailable service, live provider, production image or human pilot is marked passed. [design §7; security condition 9; ADR-SC-005 "Tests"]

docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:139:The gateway sees IDs, never values (structural: the kind has no `value` field). The DB stores IDs, vault version identifiers and audit rows. The only value-bearing channels are `BridgeDispatch.secret` (guided, mTLS + RS256) and `Launch3/Execute3.secrets` (replay, the backend→runner hop that OBS-009 makes TLS with client-certificate authentication). Runner memory holds the value from the dispatch frame until `withhold` copies it into the private inventory; wiped at `dispose`/`stop`; no scratch file, argv or env ever carries it. The browser profile is a separate disk sink neutralised by the pre-written `Preferences` file and canary-scanned. Video shows masked dots only (password-only rule); a page that later echoes a secret in plain text is a stated residual. Runner free-text sinks pass a redactor built from resolved values. Transport gates G-1 (guided mTLS), G-2 (no real credential in Vault until every secret-bearing hop is TLS-authenticated) and G-3 (no scheduled secret-referencing run before production background/secret-use authorization sources exist) are OBS-009/OBS-010 items and are **not** closed by this story.
docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/t1-pre-release-story.md:166:OBS-012A: compile-path and artifact-1 removal, `/v1/*` runner routes, v1/v2 generations and dual mount, `/api/v3` → `/api/v1/studio` move, migration re-baseline (absorbing V34), `StudioRunnerProperties` relocation. OBS-012B: frontend compile UI removal. OBS-013: recorded first Run on the persistent context created here. OBS-014: governed read/discovery policy, semantic grounding, budgets, per-action audit, retention of `progress`/`safe_result`. docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/bootstrap-closure-application/before/docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/secret-login-design.md:110:**4.2 Password-only fill (SEC-6) — ruling, restated after security review F-1.** The collector never exports a password control (§1), so the model cannot name one and the earlier "`controlType:'password'` at observation" rule was unimplementable. Rule: the model emits `fill(secretRef)` with the node-free target `{kind:"passwordControl", documentId, generation}`; **trusted runner code** resolves the target at `prepare` and again at the moment of the fill — exactly one visible, enabled `input[type=password]` in the current top-level document (frames excluded), pinned as an element handle, origin-checked (§4.3), filled through that handle so a type-flip after resolution fails on the handle. 0 or >1 candidates ⇒ `POLICY_DENIED` with reason `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT` / `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`; nothing typed. **Identity continuity (R1-1):** `generation` advances only per observation and `navigation` only on `framenavigated`, so a same-document DOM swap would otherwise let "re-resolve at fill" pick a different element. Resolution therefore runs **inside the collector's isolated world** under the existing `acquire`-style guard — cited `documentId`, `generation`, `observedNavigation === navigation` before and after the in-world call (`browser.ts:304-320`; `invoke` guard `:374`). The element pinned at `prepare` is retained in that world; the fill requires that **the same element** is still attached, still `type=password`, still the unique visible candidate, and that `location.origin` read **in that world** (not `page.url()`) is in `allowedOrigins ∩ approvedOrigins`; any deviation ⇒ `TARGET_CHANGED`, nothing typed; `navigation` is re-checked after the fill. **One function (R1-3):** "visible, enabled password input" is defined once in the isolated-world collector — computed-style visibility plus non-zero box (not viewport), traversal including open shadow roots (`observationCollector.ts:134-137,259-260,418-431`) — and that same function produces `coverage.passwordControls`, the `prepare` resolution and the fill-time check; a `querySelectorAll` resolver is forbidden. Consequences stated: an off-screen but rendered decoy counts ⇒ ambiguous ⇒ refuse; frames and closed shadow roots are excluded ⇒ absent ⇒ refuse. **Form action (R1-2):** the fill is refused with `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` when the pinned input's owning `form.action` (resolved URL) has an origin outside `allowedOrigins`, or when the input has no owning form and the document origin differs from the observed login document's origin. `GuidedProposalValidator` accepts `passwordControl` only with a `secretRef` value, only for an input whose `sourceStepId` is the fill's step, and only when the cited observation reports `coverage.passwordControls === 1`; the proposal's `executionEvidence` still binds document/generation, so staleness checks are unchanged (I-A1 holds). **Limit (stated; accepted at GA — user default 2026-10-09, ADR-SC-005):** pages with two or more visible password fields (change-password, registration with confirm) are not supported for `secretRef` fills — the author gets `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS`, nothing is typed, and there is no fallback adapter; a model-supplied ordinal/form narrowing is a reserved extension requiring its own Security review. docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBS-007/c-approved-tuple/sources/docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/contracts/v3/README.md:7:`BridgeDispatch.secret` is a closed transient object present exactly for a secret fill: ID, value (1–4096), Vault version (1–256), and 1–16 origins (each at most 512). It is excluded from digest calculation. Idempotency separately binds the safe secret ID and source input ID; it never stores a value. Replay jobs and `Execute3` carry run-scoped `secrets` and `secretOrigins`; `Launch3` carries the safe scope. `Execute3.inputs` pairs ordinary materialized entries with value-less `{inputId,stepId,kind:secretRef,intendedSlot:fill.value,referenceName}` metadata so the child resolves the declared secret ID and checks its declaring step without inferring an ID from inputId. Empty maps are valid. `Result3.secretUse` records only ID-keyed `USED`, `NOT_USED` or `REFUSED` codes. The reference grammar is `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,64}$` throughout those maps.
